Subject: Question: how backup sweep affects restores and data residency guarantees

Hi Grace,

Quick one from our infra team as we're finalizing the procurement checklist. We need to confirm two things about Redwood's backup/DR behavior for patient metadata (EU residency for a subset of records).

1) If a user-requested delete is issued (and honored in primary storage), how long before that deletion is observable in backups/replicas (tombstone propagation)? Can an expunge happen during the next periodic sweep that would make the data unrecoverable?

2) In the event we need to restore a tenant snapshot taken before a delete, what guarantees do you offer about restore fidelity and whether any tombstone/TTL logic could prevent recovery? We have a compliance window where a restored snapshot must be complete for a 30-day forensic hold.

I attached a short extract of our retention policy questions (nimbus-retention-extract-questions.pdf). Can you point us to the SLA language and any attestation artifacts?

Hi — technical summary below so you can pass back to Aisha. I'll keep the long version in the Drive folder (link below).

• Tombstone propagation: when a delete is accepted by the primary, we mark keys as tombstoned and propagate the tombstone via the same replication pipeline. For same-region replicas this is typically visible within 1–3 minutes; cross-region replication can take up to 30 minutes under normal load.

• Backup sweep vs expunge: we run a periodic expunge job (configurable per-customer) that converts tombstones into permanent deletions once the retention TTL has elapsed. The default expunge sweep runs nightly and will only remove tombstoned objects that are past their retention TTL. If a customer requests a restore of a snapshot taken before the delete and within the retention window, the tombstone policy will not prevent restoring the pre-delete state.

• Restore fidelity caveat: if a tombstone has already been converted by an expunge job (i.e., data beyond retention TTL), standard restore cannot recover the permanently deleted content. For legal holds we support retention overrides that pause expunge for affected shards — when enabled, expunge workers skip those tenant prefixes.

• Evidence/artifacts we can provide: per-snapshot manifest (manifest.json), audit log slices (tokenized for PII), expunge job run logs (screenshot-restore-job-logs.txt), and a signed attestation PDF (redwood-sla-retention-2028-03.pdf). I placed copies in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ABcdExample.

Actionable recommended answer for procurement: we can provide a written attestation and the three artifact types above. If Nimbus needs a temporary retention override for a forensic hold, we can enable that (requires a support ticket and a runbook change; typical lead time 4–8 hours).

-Karthik

Aisha — thanks for the note. Short answers for procurement: 

1) Propagation: tombstones appear in replicas within minutes (same region) and under ~30 minutes cross-region under normal conditions.
2) Expunge: periodic expunge only removes data past the customer-configured TTL. If Nimbus needs a snapshot restored that predates a delete and the data is still within TTL, restore will succeed.

What we'll deliver:
- Signed attestation describing retention and expunge behavior (PDF)
- Per-snapshot manifest for the requested tenant
- Audit log slice showing the delete + tombstone propagation timestamps

If you want a formal SLA clause we can include the propagation window and expunge scheduling in the contract; procurement, let us know if you want the retention override clause (it documents the 4–8 hour enablement window).
